findings.F1: The book's whole gain comes from its long side. Long bars summed +6.32 in gain before fees against 1.13 in fees. Short bars summed −0.36 before fees and paid another 0.79 in fees, so after fees the shorts are a net loss of about 1.14 over 8,517 bars.
findings.F2: Removing the shorts repairs the failing Calmar but not the mean. A long-only version of the same book has mean daily return 0.000296 against 0.000229, Sharpe 1.02 against 0.61, deepest fall −13.3% against −19.8%, and Calmar 0.81 against 0.39 (the rule needs 0.75).
findings.F3: The lowest forecast quintile does not lead to falling coins. It sits 1.07% below the coin's 7-day mean, yet its raw 7-day return is −0.14%, and the bars held short rose on average (+0.0068% a day). The deep-below, thin-volume side forecasts relative weakness, not an absolute fall.
findings.F4: Only the top forecast quintile carries real gains: +1.84% in 7-day excess return (+2.75% raw), with 0.155% daily gain per bar. The next quintile earns 0.026% a day and the lower three about 0 or negative.
findings.F5: Shorts lose most where the coin trends hardest. In the top 60-day-return quartile (+79% on average) shorts lose −0.029% a day, and in the bottom quartile (−36%) they lose −0.021% a day. Shorts gain only in the mildly falling quartile (+0.062%).
findings.F6: The graded relation is stronger when the coin is rising over 60 days, and so are the long gains:

ideas.idea: The closer a coin's daily close sits to its highest close of the past 20 days, and the heavier that day's volume against its 30-day average, the higher the coin's return over the next 7 days, only while the coin's own 60-day return is positive, the gain growing with both closeness and volume inside that rising state.
ideas.consequence: Hold larger longs in coins pressing their 20-day high on heavy volume during a rising 60-day trend, and do not read a close far below the high as a reason to short.
ideas.name: Near-high volume in uptrends

ideas.idea: The closer a coin's daily close sits to its highest close of the past 20 days, and the heavier that day's volume against its 30-day average, the larger the coin's rise over the next 7 days, the move being an absolute gain that grows with closeness and volume, while closes far below the high on thin volume are followed by smaller rises rather than falls.
ideas.consequence: Read the signal as a long-only scale from flat to a full long, never taking a short when the close sits deep below the high.
ideas.name: Near-high is long-only
